analyst_view.overall: Early view: Arsenal are 3rd with 10 points and top of the Premier League, but they are winning narrowly: 1-0 at Liverpool, 2-1 at Slavia Prague (a win Mikel Arteta called sloppy) and 1-0 against Hull. Borussia Dortmund (12th, 9 points) beat Real Betis 2-1 on matchday 4 and drew 2-2 at Bayern before that, so they are in decent form; William Saliba is building fitness again after his World Cup injury, which would strengthen Arsenal further.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and I lean lower. Arsenal's last three games ended 1-0, 2-1 and 1-0, and Arteta himself said his side must stop chasing the perfect goal, which tells you the attack is the issue rather than the defence. With Saliba close to a return, a low-scoring home win fits the pattern better than an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I lean slightly higher. When Arsenal struggle to break teams down they keep recycling the ball wide and win corners, and their set pieces are a big part of how they create. Dortmund are likely to defend deep for long spells at the Emirates.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and I lean higher. Dortmund picked up five yellow cards against Betis (Julian Ryerson, Ramy Bensebaini, Joey Veerman and Jobe Bellingham among them), and Arsenal had two booked at Slavia. Arsenal's edge in big games, the 'dark arts' debate around them, tends to draw fouls and bookings from opponents.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots and I stay with it. Arsenal will have most of the ball and plenty of attempts, but their recent games have been tight rather than shot-heavy, and Dortmund are good enough to keep it to a measured total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Arsenal's attack has lacked a focal point (Viktor Gyokeres only found form at Slavia), and Arteta has spoken about his side being too careful in the final third. Dortmund's own threat away from home should be limited.
